conclusions: The actual native access is now proven to be an ordinary unaligned halfword Load in the cached aperture. It is not yet proven to target PSRAM rather than Flash.

The current internal-only eligibility guard explains the source-level Unsupported boundary before cache/MMU/perms, but actual mapping and gate validity must be checked before claiming this access can succeed.

TRM ordinary scalar splitting plus the external D-bus/cache/MMU path supports a bounded functional same-page contiguous mapped-memory subset, preserving all existing protections and actual source/die gates.
The previous internal-only scope was a deliberate model boundary, not a silicon prohibition on ordinary unaligned external memory.
No MISALIGN/UNALIGN control was found in the four fetched fixed553 headers;553/554 csr.h and soc.h are byte-identical. MHINT.SBE changes error synchrony, not alignment permission.
The official emulator public pinned docs do not provide a C5 ordinary-unaligned core implementation or trap contract. Its flash cache backing shortcut is not proof of physical split behavior.
